summary: Clarifies the GMPLS signaling procedures for controlling the label used on the output interface of the egress node of a Label Switched Path, known as Egress Control.

plainLanguage.summary: This RFC clarifies how GMPLS signaling handles the outgoing interface and label at the end of a Label Switched Path. It restates how the egress node interprets the route information for unidirectional and bidirectional paths.

subtitle: Clarifying how a GMPLS egress node handles its outgoing interface and label.

tldr.problem: Earlier GMPLS text did not make clear how the egress-control procedures applied to labels on an egress output interface.
tldr.mechanism: This RFC clarifies how an egress node uses interface and label subobjects in an Explicit Route Object and records them in a Route Record Object when indicated.
tldr.outcome: It clarifies RFC 3473 procedures without changing GMPLS signaling mechanisms or procedures.

today: RFC 4003 is a Standards Track document that updates RFC 3473. It clarifies egress-control procedures for GMPLS signaling.

sections.title: Why Egress Control Needed Clarification
sections.content:
Egress Control means controlling the label used on the output or downstream interface of a Label Switched Path's egress node. The GMPLS specifications generalized label control to any interface, but the intended procedures for the egress interface were not clear to all readers.

RFC 4003 reiterates how the existing signaling procedures apply to this case. It does not change GMPLS signaling mechanisms or procedures.
sections.plainLanguage: The RFC explains how existing GMPLS rules apply when a path reaches its final node. Its purpose is to make the egress-label behavior clear.

sections.title: Reading Interface and Label Information
sections.content:
Egress Control applies when the node processing an Explicit Route Object (ERO) is the egress and the ERO contains information about an outgoing interface. The egress identifies the last listed local interface and examines the following subobjects. It examines one subobject for a unidirectional LSP and two for a bidirectional LSP.

If the examined subobject's U-bit is clear, the label value MUST be used for traffic sent on the indicated interface. If the U-bit is set, the label value is used for upstream traffic associated with the bidirectional LSP.
sections.plainLanguage: The egress node checks the route information for its outgoing interface and the labels that follow it. The U-bit tells the node whether a label applies to sent traffic or upstream traffic.

sections.title: Errors and Route Recording
sections.content: If a listed label is unacceptable or cannot be supported for forwarding, the egress SHOULD send a PathErr message with the Routing Error code and Bad Explicit Route Object value. When label recording is indicated, the egress should include the specified interface and label information in the corresponding Route Record Object.
sections.plainLanguage: If the egress cannot use the requested label, it should report a routing error. When the path is being recorded, it should include the interface and label information.

sections.title: Security Considerations
sections.content: The RFC says it clarifies procedures already defined in RFC 3473 and does not define new procedures. It therefore introduces no new security considerations.
sections.plainLanguage: This clarification adds no new signaling procedures, so the RFC identifies no new security considerations.

references.text: Berger, L., "Generalized Multi-Protocol Label Switching (GMPLS) Signaling Resource Reservation Protocol-Traffic Engineering (RSVP-TE) Extensions", RFC 3473, January 2003.
